name: Svoi Kozyri
description: Svoi Kozyri (Russian: 'My Own Trumps' or 'Your Trumps') is a Russian card game where players have their own personal trump suit. It is a shedding game for 2-4 players. The objective is to get rid of all your cards. The twist is that if you lead a card of your own trump suit, it is powerful for you, but attacking others with their trumps forces them to defend heavily.

history.origins: Svoi Kozyri (Russian: "one's own trumps") is a single-attack beating game; the earliest printed descriptions date from the 19th century. It survived as Vsyak svoi kozyri ("everyone has their own trumps") though rarely played today. Some sources consider it an elaboration of the Czech game Sedma. A two-player variant was brought to Cambridge by mathematician A.S. Besikovitch and published as "Challenge" in the Pan Book of Card Games; it was reportedly popular in Belarus in the countryside.
history.evolution: The concept of 'private trumps' is unique.

setup.players: Two, three, or four players; best for four. Each player has a different trump suit agreed before play.
setup.deck: Standard Russian 36-card pack: A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6 in each of the four French suits.
setup.dealing: Any player deals first; then the loser of each hand deals. Dealer shuffles, optional cut by player to dealer's right, then deals all 36 cards clockwise one at a time. Before play, players with sixes give them to the player who has that suit as trumps so each player has at least one trump.

rules.objective: Get rid of all your cards. The last player left holding cards is the loser.
rules.gameplay: Play is clockwise. The player to the left of the dealer leads any card face-up to start the play pile. On your turn you may either beat the top card (play a higher card of the same suit or one of your own trumps on a different suit) and then play a second card of your choice on top, or pick up cards from the pile (3 if the top is not your trump, 5 if it is your trump but not the ace, or the whole pile if it is the ace of your trump). After a pick-up, the next player must beat the new top card or pick up. If the pile is empty, the next player leads any card. Each player has one assigned trump suit; only your own trumps can beat other suits.
keyRules: Each player has a different trump suit agreed before play.
Before play, players give any sixes to the player who has that suit as trumps.
Beat with higher same suit or your trump; then play a second card.
Cannot or will not beat: pick up 3, 5, or whole pile depending on top card.
Last player holding cards loses and deals the next hand.

strategy.basic: Hoard your trumps. If you have the Ace of your suit, it's unbeatable by anyone except... nobody? Actually, if you lead it, someone else might trump it with their trump? No, usually your trump beats their non-trump. Trumps vs Trumps? Usually standard rank.
strategy.intermediate: Attack the Trump: Lead the opponent's trump suit to force them to play high trumps or pick up.
strategy.advanced: Memory: Know which high cards of your suit are out. If the King is gone, your Queen is boss.
tips: Don't waste it on small attacks.

variations.name: Regional pick-up counts
variations.description: The number of cards picked up when not beating varies in different parts of Russia (e.g. 3, 5, or whole pile).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Regional rules differ only in pick-up counts; no engine overrides needed for current build.

variations.name: Besikovich's game
variations.description: Two-player variant with all cards exposed and symmetric deal; alternative to beating is to take the whole play pile. Published as Challenge in Pan Book of Card Games.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant uses different deal and visibility; overrides can be added when implementing this variant.

scoring.description: Empty hand; last player holding cards loses.
